methodological_rigor.justification: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II/III trial with central randomization, stratification by PD-L1 CPS and HPV status, pre-specified primary endpoints (OS and PFS), and a pre-specified 2-in-1 adaptive design with explicit IDMC futility criteria (ΔORR<0% and ΔDCR<0%). Sample size was event-driven with a prespecified calculation (374 patients, 53% PD-L1 CPS≥20 prevalence), analytical methods were appropriate (stratified log-rank, Cox PH with Efron tie-handling, Miettinen–Nurminen for ORR/DCR), and the mITT and safety populations are clearly defined. Limitations include immature data at the futility stop (median follow-up 6.28 months, high early censoring acknowledged in Discussion), lack of exposure-adjusted safety analysis explicitly noted, p-values not presented at interim, and the ctDNA/biomarker subgroup findings are post hoc with modest sample sizes (BEP1 n=145, BEP2 n=97). Overall, methods are solid and transparently reported, with limitations fairly disclosed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II/III trial, mapping to Oxford LoE 1b. The patient-relevant endpoints (OS, PFS, ORR, HRQoL via EORTC and PROMIS-PF8c) in a defined 1L R/M HNSCC population directly inform clinical decision-making. Although the trial is negative, it is clinically consequential: it eliminates ICOS agonism via feladilimab from the HNSCC development pipeline (authors state no further investigation is planned), reinforces a pattern of failed anti-PD-1 combinations in HNSCC, and contributes a cautionary message about advancing from single-arm Phase I signals to Phase III. The exploratory ctDNA stratification hypothesis is translationally interesting but speculative.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this RCT. The manuscript reports trial registration (NCT04128696), eligibility, randomization and blinding methodology, stratification factors, pre-specified endpoints, interim/futility rules, a patient-flow figure (Fig. 1), AE/SAE reporting, protocol amendment history (May 19, 2020), and reasons for early discontinuation. Minor gaps include limited numerical detail on allocation concealment mechanics and lack of an explicit CONSORT checklist reference. Data and code availability are not described in the manuscript text (no deposition identifier, no analytic code location, no biomarker raw-data repository stated), and vendor-generated assay data are proprietary — consistent with industry trials but limiting reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty lies in being, to the authors' framing, a definitive randomized evaluation of an ICOS agonist (feladilimab) combined with pembrolizumab in 1L PD-L1+ R/M HNSCC — a target/combination not previously tested in a randomized setting in this disease. However, this is empirically a confirmatory negative result that joins a cluster of negative anti-PD-1 combination trials in HNSCC (CheckMate 651, KESTREL, EAGLE, KEYNOTE-669/ECHO-304) that the authors themselves cite. The exploratory ctDNA-stratified differential effect and integrated germline PRS/HLA biomarker analyses add modest methodological interest. Overall, this is a meaningful but incremental contribution rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized and clearly written, with a self-contained abstract that quantitatively summarizes the key efficacy signals (adjusted HRs 1.51 for OS, 1.40 for PFS) and the IDMC futility decision. The Introduction effectively motivates the ICOS target and the INDUCE-1 signal, Methods are detailed, and the Discussion thoughtfully situates the negative finding alongside other failed HNSCC immunotherapy combinations and offers mechanistic hypotheses (regulatory T-cell stimulation, PD-L1/ICOS-L inverse expression). Figure and table captions are informative and standalone-interpretable; acronyms are generally defined on first use. Minor awkwardness in the adaptive-criteria section (duplicated bullet text) and some density in the biomarker Methods subsection.

key_strengths: Rigorous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II/III design with prespecified 2-in-1 adaptive futility rules and IDMC-driven stopping (LoE 1b)
Transparent reporting of a negative trial with clinically consequential implications — informs discontinuation of feladilimab development in HNSCC
Appropriate stratified log-rank/Cox analyses, Miettinen–Nurminen ORR/DCR estimation, and clear mITT/safety population definitions
Thoughtful integration of exploratory biomarkers (ctDNA, TMB, germline PRS, HLA, TIS) with honest acknowledgment of their post hoc, hypothesis-generating nature
Discussion productively contextualizes the result alongside other failed HNSCC immunotherapy combinations and offers plausible mechanistic hypotheses
key_concerns: Immature data at the futility analysis (median follow-up 6.28 months, high early censoring) limits interpretation of OS curves, particularly the dramatic HR of 4.44 in the CPS≥20 subgroup
No data/code availability statement; biomarker raw data and analytic pipelines not deposited
Exposure-adjusted safety analysis explicitly omitted despite relevant TRAE differences between arms
Novelty is incremental — joins a sequence of similar negative anti-PD-1 combination trials in HNSCC
Duplicated/awkward presentation of the adaptive decision criteria and some unpublished biomarker threshold derivations (EORTC IL51 pain, PROMIS-PF8c) cited as 'unpublished data'
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorously conducted negative Phase II/III RCT with clinical importance for the HNSCC immunotherapy landscape — fits well within Tier 2 (e.g., Clinical Cancer Research / Cancer Research–level) given solid methodology and translational relevance but incremental scientific contribution and immature follow-up.
